details.label: Status
details.text: `[FACT]`: failed in both PR Tests on Nov 21 (rocm10 at 01:10 and rocm724 at 04:12), in shard 2. On Nov 20 13:10 the file passed in shard 1.

New unit files from [#51939](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/51939), [#50806](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/50806) and [#51464](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/51464) took the suite from 434 to 437 files. That moved both files into the same shard.

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` [#46029](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46029) ([`ba9c86bb`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/ba9c86bb7eee016a3d5943f4dfe3d8daf0ad7e0a)) added `test_npu_falls_back_from_pipelined_attention`. It patches the lazy attribute with `monkeypatch.setattr(platforms, "current_platform", …)` at `test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py:702`.
On teardown, pytest 9.0.3 writes the real ROCm platform back as a module attribute. That attribute hides the module `__getattr__`, so later patches of `platforms._current_platform` do nothing.
What the tests then see: dispatch through `forward_hip`, and `nccl` where the mock returns `gloo`.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: the mechanism was reproduced with a toy module, not by running the two real files together on ROCm.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ❌ none found. [#51734](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/51734) (open since Nov 20) isolates other unit tests from the real platform but does not cover line 702.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: run `pytest …/test_minimax_h3_dit_contract.py::test_npu_falls_back_from_pipelined_attention …/test_oot_platform_runtime.py` in the CI image. The pair should fail and the second file alone should pass. If so, patch `platforms._current_platform` at line 702.
